Fit a mixed model per feature on a latent scale, from samples measured on it, counted through it, or both

stats_fit_latent_mixed.Rd

Fit one random-intercept mixed model per feature on a latent scale (such as the log-odds of a site's occupancy), where each sample is either measured on that scale or counted through it (k of n trials succeed), and test each named coefficient with a Wald t.

Answers does a value follow a trait, when some runs measured it and others only counted successes, k of n? A PTM site's occupancy is the usual case: where the modified and unmodified peptides were both quantified you have a number; where they were not, you may know only that 3 of 8 covering peptidoforms carried the modification. stats_fit_mixed has to drop the counted runs. This uses both kinds.

Usage

stats_fit_latent_mixed(design, groups, coefficients, link, responses = NULL,
  counts = NULL, depth = NULL, residual_variance = NULL, estimator = NULL, threads = 1,
  timeout = 600)

Arguments

design

stats_fit's design: a TSV with a header row and one row per sample, the sample name then one numeric column per fixed-effect coefficient. Do not add a column per group: the random intercept replaces it. mzLib refuses a design that is not of full column rank.

groups

stats_fit_mixed's groups table: one row per sample, the sample name then ONE column with its group label (an animal, a donor, a dataset), whose header names the grouping.

coefficients

Design column names to report, each as one block of rows, sent one per stdin line. Every design column is fitted whatever you name.

link

mzLib's DetectionLink, in natural log-odds: "identity" (DetectionLink.Identity, intercept 0 and slope 1: a count samples the same probability a measurement reads), a stats_fit_link result or its $link, or 2 to 4 numbers c(intercept, slope[, depth_slope[, overdispersion]]), sent as given: a value you leave out is mzLib's default (0 at the pin). Required: mzLib has no default link.

responses

The measured samples, in latent units (logit occupancy, for example, not a fraction): stats_fit_mixed's responses table, a TSV with the feature id first and one column per sample. Blank, NA or NaN is not measured. Give responses, counts or both. NULL (the default): nothing was measured.

counts

The counted samples, in trials: a table laid out as responses, each cell successes/trials (3/8), or blank where the sample was not counted. With responses too, the two must list the same features and samples, and no cell may be in both. NULL (the default): nothing was counted, and the model is stats_fit_mixed's.

depth

A TSV with a header row and one row per sample: the sample name, then its depth in your depth units (log2 target PSMs, say), for the link's depth term. Needed when the link's depth_slope is not 0. NULL (the default): none is sent.

residual_variance

A TSV with a header row and one row per feature: the feature id, then sigma^2 to use for it (squared latent units) instead of estimating it, for a feature with too few measured samples. Blank, or a feature not listed, is estimated. NULL (the default): every sigma^2 is estimated.

estimator

"reml" or "ml". Leave it NULL (the default) for mzLib's default ("reml" at the pin); estimator in the result says which was used.

threads

Features fitted at once (threads), or -1 for every core. The answer is identical at any value.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL to wait indefinitely.

Details

mzLib's LogitNormalMixedModel.Fit (mzLib #1469) is stats_fit_mixed's model - fixed effects from your design, one baseline per group drawn from N(0, tau^2), run-to-run scatter sigma^2 - on a latent value, such as the log-odds of a site's occupancy. A sample can be measured (its latent value is in responses) or counted: k of its n trials succeeded (counts), each with a chance g set by the latent value through the link, logit g = intercept + slope x latent + depth_slope x depth. It is lme4::glmer (a binomial GLMM, with an observation-level random effect for sigma^2) and lmer in one model, which mzLib checks against both and against glmmTMB.

Which cells are counted, and the link, are your choices: mzLibR builds neither. stats_fit_link fits a link from cells.

Value

An mzlibr_latent_mixed_model_fit:

- records, a data.frame with one row per (reported coefficient, feature) - one block of feature_count rows per coefficient you named, in that order, each in the feature order of the responses file (of the counts file, without one): feature; coefficient; status, one of "fitted", "too_few_observations", "rank_deficient", "separated" (no finite estimate exists: a status, never a p-value), "not_converged" or "too_few_groups"; estimate, the fixed effect within groups on the latent scale (latent units per coefficient unit: natural log-odds for a logit latent, so exp(estimate) is an odds ratio); standard_error (latent units per coefficient unit), from the inverse Hessian at the estimated variances; df (degrees of freedom), nlme's containment df over the samples with a response of either kind, NA when not fitted or when no positive df exists; t (standard errors), the Wald statistic; p_value, a fraction (0 to 1), two-sided on df, not adjusted across features, NA also when df is; residual_variance (squared latent units), sigma^2, run to run within a group, estimated or the one you gave; residual_variance_given, TRUE when it is the one you gave; group_variance (squared latent units), tau^2, where 0 is the boundary; log_likelihood (log-likelihood, natural log), Laplace-approximated restricted under "reml", full under "ml"; measured, samples with a finite response (samples); counted, samples with a count (samples); and groups, distinct groups among both (groups). Statistics are NA where status is not "fitted". - responses_file, counts_file, depth_file and residual_variance_file (NA when not given), design_file and groups_file, as absolute paths; grouping, the groups file's label column header; group_names, in order of first appearance; group_count groups; feature_count features and sample_count samples read; sample_names; coefficient_names and tested_coefficients; estimator, the estimator mzLib used; link, the link every count was read through, as mzLib reports it: an mzlibr_detection_link with intercept (natural log-odds), slope (natural log-odds per latent unit), depth_slope (natural log-odds per depth unit) and overdispersion (fraction, the intra-cell correlation, 0 to below 1); threads (threads); measured_cells, counted_cells and missing_count (cells); status_counts, features per status (features); row_count rows; column_names. - caveats: what the model is and is not, the link and the estimator used, plus counts for this input: unfitted features, rows with no df, features at the boundary, residual variances given.

What it is not

A random intercept per group and nothing more: no random slopes, nested or crossed groupings. Responses and estimates are on the latent scale, never fractions or intensities. Standard errors are at the estimated variances and do not include their uncertainty, so they are not glmmTMB's vcov(). Under "reml" the fixed effects are integrated out by a Laplace approximation, as glmmTMB's REML = TRUE does; with nothing counted it is exactly stats_fit_mixed's REML, and the two agree to about 1e-5. Send one coefficient's p_value column to stats_adjust for Benjamini-Hochberg.

Wraps

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

responses

path; in latent units (e.g. natural log-odds of occupancy); default absent. The measured samples: stats fit-mixed's responses table, a TSV with a header row, the feature id first (unique) and then one column per sample, named by its header. Values are on the LATENT scale (logit occupancy, for example), not fractions or intensities. A blank cell, NA or NaN (any case) is not measured. At least one of responses and counts is required. Absent, no sample is measured: the bridge passes an all-missing matrix of the counts' shape.

counts

path; in trials (successes of trials); default absent; range each cell k/n, two whole numbers. The counted samples (mzLib's BinomialCount): a TSV laid out as responses, each cell successes/trials such as 3/8, or blank, NA or NaN for a sample not counted. When both tables are given they must list exactly the same feature ids and sample columns, in any order (the responses' order is kept), and a cell may be measured or counted, not both (mzLib's rule). mzLib refuses a count with no trials, or more successes than trials. Absent, no sample is counted, and the model is stats fit-mixed's.

design

path; required. stats fit's design table: one row per sample, the sample name (matching the fit's sample columns exactly, rows matched by name) then one column per fixed-effect coefficient, every cell a finite number. Include an intercept column if you want one; do not add a column per group, which the random intercept replaces. mzLib refuses a design that is not of full column rank over all samples.

groups

path; required. stats fit-mixed's groups table: one row per sample, the sample name then EXACTLY ONE column, the sample's group label (an animal, a donor, a dataset), whose header names the grouping. The sample names must be exactly the fit's sample columns. Labels are trimmed and compared exactly; mzLib refuses an empty one.

link

string; in natural log-odds; required; range identity, or 2 to 4 comma-separated numbers: intercept,slope[,depth_slope[,overdispersion]]. mzLib's DetectionLink: how the latent value sets the chance g that one trial of a counted cell succeeds, logit g = intercept + slope x latent + depth_slope x depth, with trials in a cell correlated by overdispersion (rho, a beta-binomial; 0 is the binomial). REQUIRED: mzLib's link parameter has no default. identity is DetectionLink.Identity, (0, 1): a counted cell then samples the same probability a measured one reads. Numbers are passed as the record's positional arguments, so a depth_slope or overdispersion left out is the record's own default (0 at cc67b7a2). stats fit-link fits one from cells. mzLib refuses a non-finite intercept or depth slope, a slope that is 0 or not finite, and an overdispersion outside [0, 1).

depth

path; in depth units (the caller's, e.g. log2 target PSMs); default absent. A TSV with a header row and one row per sample: the sample name (exactly the fit's samples, in any order), then one number, the sample's depth for the link's depth term. Needed when the link's depth_slope is not 0 (mzLib refuses otherwise). Absent, the bridge passes none.

residual_variance (wire --residual-variance)

path; in squared latent units; default absent; range each > 0 and finite, or blank to estimate. A TSV with a header row and one row per feature: the feature id, then sigma^2 to use for it instead of estimating it (e.g. borrowed when a feature has too few measured samples). A blank, NA or NaN cell, or a feature not listed, is NaN, which mzLib reads as estimate it. An id that is not one of the fit's features is refused. Absent, the bridge passes none and every sigma^2 is estimated.

coefficients (wire --stdin)

string[]; required; range >= 1 line; each a design column name, none repeated. The coefficients to report, one design column name per line. The model always fits every design column; the table holds one block of rows per coefficient named here, in this order.

estimator

string; default absent; range reml | ml. reml is VarianceEstimator.Reml (the fixed effects integrated out by a Laplace approximation, as glmmTMB's REML; exact when nothing is counted), ml is VarianceEstimator.MaximumLikelihood. Absent, the bridge sends none and LogitNormalMixedModel.Fit's default applies (Reml at cc67b7a2); the envelope's estimator says which was used.

threads

int; in threads; default 1; range >= 1, or -1 for every core. Features fitted at once. The bridge default is 1 (BULK.md); mzLib's own default is -1. Results are identical at any value (mzLib).

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

responses_file

string; NA when no --responses: nothing was measured. Absolute path of the responses table.

counts_file

string; NA when no --counts: nothing was counted. Absolute path of the counts table.

design_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the design table.

groups_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the groups table.

depth_file

string; NA when no --depth was given. Absolute path of the depth table.

residual_variance_file

string; NA when no --residual-variance: every sigma^2 was estimated. Absolute path of the residual-variance table.

grouping

string; never NA. The groups file's label column header.

group_names

string[]; never NA. The distinct labels, in order of first appearance over the samples (the order mzLib numbers them in).

group_count

int; in groups; never NA. Distinct labels over all samples. A feature's own count is its groups column.

feature_count

int; in features; never NA. Feature rows read.

sample_count

int; in samples; never NA. Sample columns read.

sample_names

string[]; never NA. In the responses header's order (the counts header's, with counts alone): the order the design, group and depth rows were put in.

coefficient_names

string[]; never NA. Every design column, in order.

tested_coefficients

string[]; never NA. The stdin coefficients, in order; the table holds one block of feature_count rows per entry.

estimator

string; never NA. reml or ml: the estimator mzLib reports it fitted with (LogitNormalMixedModelFit.Estimator), the default when --estimator was absent.

link

object; never NA. The link every count cell was read through, as mzLib reports it (LogitNormalMixedModelFit.Link); fields under result.tables.link.

threads

int; in threads; never NA. The thread count used.

measured_cells

int; in cells; never NA. Feature x sample cells with a finite response.

counted_cells

int; in cells; never NA. Feature x sample cells with a count.

missing_count

int; in cells; never NA. Cells with neither a response nor a count, left out of their feature's fit.

status_counts

map<string,int>; in features; never NA. Features per status, always these six keys: fitted, too_few_observations, rank_deficient, separated, not_converged, too_few_groups. They are the outcomes LogitNormalMixedModel.Fit's body can return at cc67b7a2; a stop-gap until mzLib says per model (mzLib#1487).

row_count

int; in rows; never NA. feature_count x the number of tested coefficients.

column_names

string[]; never NA. The table's columns, in order.

records (wire columns)

table; never NA. One row per (tested coefficient, feature): coefficient blocks in stdin order, features in file order.

caveats

string[]; never NA. Seven static caveats (one names the link used, one the estimator), plus one each, with counts, when any feature was not fitted, when a fitted row has no df, when a fitted feature's group_variance is 0, when any residual variance was given, and when nothing was counted.

Columns of records

feature

string; never NA. The feature id from the first column.

coefficient

string; never NA. The coefficient this row reports.

status

string; never NA. fitted | too_few_observations (no more samples with a response of either kind than coefficients) | rank_deficient (the design over those samples is not of full rank) | separated (no estimate exists: a coefficient beyond +-SeparationLimit, 30 at cc67b7a2, on the latent scale, a Hessian that is not positive definite, or nothing measured and every group's counts one-sided, all 0 or all full) | not_converged (the variance search failed, or the likelihood could not be evaluated at its optimum) | too_few_groups (fewer than two groups, or none with two samples). Only fitted rows carry statistics.

estimate

float; in latent units per coefficient unit (natural log-odds for a logit latent); NA when status is not fitted. The fixed-effect coefficient at the estimated variances: the effect within groups, on the latent scale.

standard_error

float; in latent units per coefficient unit; NA when not fitted. sqrt of the diagonal of H^-1, H = -d2 l / d beta2 at the estimate (l the log-likelihood with the random effects integrated out). With nothing counted, (X' V^-1 X)^-1 as stats fit-mixed reports under reml.

df

float; in degrees of freedom; NA when not fitted, or the containment df is not positive (a group-level coefficient with too few groups). Denominator df of the t test, by nlme's containment rule over the samples with a response of either kind, a whole number.

t

float; in standard errors; NA when not fitted. Wald statistic, estimate / standard_error. Reported even when df is null.

p_value

float; in fraction (0 to 1); NA when not fitted, or df is null. Two-sided p-value of the t test on df. Not adjusted across features.

residual_variance

float; in squared latent units; NA when not fitted. sigma^2, the run-to-run variance of the latent within a group: estimated, or the value given (residual_variance_given). The same in every coefficient block.

residual_variance_given

bool; never NA. True when residual_variance is the value the --residual-variance file gave, not an estimate. Reported whatever the status.

group_variance

float; in squared latent units; NA when not fitted. tau^2, the between-group variance of the random intercept. 0 is the boundary estimate. The same in every coefficient block.

log_likelihood

float; in log-likelihood (natural log); NA when not fitted. The maximized log-likelihood: under reml the Laplace-approximated restricted likelihood (exactly the restricted likelihood when nothing is counted), under ml the full one. The same in every coefficient block.

measured

int; in samples; never NA. Samples with a finite response for this feature.

counted

int; in samples; never NA. Samples with a count for this feature.

groups

int; in groups; never NA. Distinct groups among this feature's samples with a response of either kind.

Fields of link

an mzlibr_detection_link, a named list of these four numbers.

link$intercept (wire intercept)

float; in natural log-odds; never NA. a: the per-trial log-odds at latent 0 and depth 0.

link$slope (wire slope)

float; in natural log-odds per latent unit; never NA. b: how fast the per-trial log-odds follow the latent; 1 for the identity link, below 1 when the chance of a success rises more slowly than the latent.

link$depth_slope (wire depth_slope)

float; in natural log-odds per depth unit; never NA. c: the depth term's coefficient; 0 when the link has none.

link$overdispersion (wire overdispersion)

float; in fraction (intra-cell correlation, 0 to < 1); never NA. rho, the correlation of trials within one cell (beta-binomial); 0 is the binomial.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

neither --responses nor --counts; design, groups or link missing; a file given without a value or not found; a table empty, header-only or with too few columns; a row whose field count differs from its header; an empty or repeated feature id, sample or coefficient name; a response cell that is not a number (other than blank, NA, NaN); a count cell that is not two whole numbers k/n; a design cell that is not a finite number

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

the counts' features or samples are not exactly the responses' (each difference named); the design's, the groups' or the depth file's samples are not exactly the fit's; the groups or depth file with other than two columns; a depth that is not a number; a residual-variance id that is not a feature, or a value that is not a number; no coefficient on stdin, one named twice, or one not in the design; --link not identity or 2 to 4 numbers; --estimator other than reml or ml; --threads 0 or below -1

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

mzLib refuses the input (its ArgumentException, reclassified): a cell both measured and counted, or a count with no trials or more successes than trials, named by 0-based position and then by feature and sample name; a link with a slope of 0, a non-finite value or overdispersion outside [0, 1); a link with a depth term and no --depth; a depth that is not finite; a given residual variance that is not positive and finite; a design not of full column rank; an empty group label

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

never expected

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • A random intercept per group on a latent scale: a measured sample reads the latent; a counted sample has k of n trials succeed with logit g = intercept + slope x latent + depth_slope x depth, binomially or beta-binomially. No random slopes, nested or crossed groupings.

  • Responses and estimates are on the latent scale (natural log-odds for a logit latent), not fractions or intensities. Which cells are counted, and the link, are the caller's modelling choices; the bridge builds neither (stats fit-link fits a link).

  • Counted samples are integrated by adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature (40 nodes over the group intercept, 12 over each count's residual), measured ones exactly. mzLib agrees with lme4's glmer (nAGQ 25, ML) to about 1e-6, with lmer to about 1e-5 when nothing is counted, and with glmmTMB to its Laplace error (about 1% in tau^2 and standard errors, 5% in sigma^2) when sigma^2 is estimated from counts alone (ReferenceComparisonLogitNormalTests).

  • Fixed effects are tested by Wald t on nlme's containment df, over samples with a response of either kind. standard_error is at the estimated variances and does not include their uncertainty, so it is not glmmTMB's vcov().

  • Under reml the fixed effects are integrated out by a Laplace approximation (glmmTMB's REML = TRUE); it is exact when nothing is counted. Under REML glmmTMB reports beta as the joint mode of (beta, u), so compare its estimates with this verb's ml ones only.

  • With nothing counted the model is stats fit-mixed's, fitted by a different optimiser: under reml the numbers agree with fit-mixed's to about 1e-5; under ml estimates and variances agree, but standard errors are at the ML variances, where fit-mixed's scale by RSS / (observed - coefficients) as nlme's summary does.

  • separated is a status, never a p-value: the counts are (quasi-)completely separated by the design and the estimate runs to infinity.

  • p_value is not adjusted across features. Send one coefficient's p_value column to stats adjust for Benjamini-Hochberg.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::stats::fit_latent_mixed_with with FitLatentMixedOptions

  • R (mzLibR): stats_fit_latent_mixed

References

  • doi:10.1080/01621459.1993.10594284: generalized linear mixed models, the class of model this verb fits: a latent linear predictor with a random intercept, observed through a binomial link (Breslow and Clayton, J Am Stat Assoc 88:9, 1993)

  • doi:10.1093/biomet/81.3.624: adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature, centred at the integrand's mode and scaled by its curvature, which mzLib uses to integrate the counted samples (Liu and Pierce, Biometrika 81:624, 1994)

  • doi:10.18637/jss.v067.i01: lme4's lmer and glmer (nAGQ 25), the references mzLib's fits are held to (Bates, Maechler, Bolker and Walker, J Stat Softw 67:1, 2015)

  • doi:10.32614/RJ-2017-066: glmmTMB, whose Laplace-approximated REML mzLib's REML follows and whose fits with run scatter are a reference (Brooks et al., R Journal 9:378, 2017)

  • doi:10.1093/biomet/58.3.545: restricted maximum likelihood, the default estimator (Patterson and Thompson, Biometrika 58:545, 1971)

  • doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1948.tb00014.x: the beta-binomial distribution, which a link with overdispersion gives a count cell (Skellam, J R Stat Soc B 10:257, 1948)

See also

stats_fit_link for the link, stats_fit_mixed when every sample is measured

Examples


# mzLib's own reference input: 16 simulated features, 23 samples in 8 animals, every sample
# counted, read through the link (-0.4, 0.6, 0.3) with a depth term; and lme4's glmer() fit of it
# (25-point adaptive quadrature, maximum likelihood), which this package ships.
data <- system.file("extdata", "stats", package = "mzLibR")
fit <- stats_fit_latent_mixed(file.path(data, "lnmm_reference_design.tsv"),
  file.path(data, "lnmm_reference_groups.tsv"), c("Intercept", "trait", "x"),
  link = c(-0.4, 0.6, 0.3), counts = file.path(data, "lnmm_link_counts.tsv"),
  depth = file.path(data, "lnmm_link_depth.tsv"),
  residual_variance = file.path(data, "lnmm_link_residual_variance.tsv"), estimator = "ml")
fit
#> <mzlibr_latent_mixed_model_fit> 16 features x 23 samples in 8 groups (group), ml, reporting Intercept, trait, x
#>   0 measured and 338 counted cells, through logit g = -0.4 + 0.6 x latent + 0.3 x depth, overdispersion 0
#>   fitted 16, too_few_observations 0, rank_deficient 0, separated 0, not_converged 0, too_few_groups 0
trait <- fit$records[fit$records$coefficient == "trait", ]
glmer <- read.delim(file.path(data, "lnmm_counted_fit.tsv"))
glmer <- glmer[glmer$link == "link" & glmer$method == "ML", ]
# Every trait estimate is within 1e-5 standard errors of glmer's:
max(abs(trait$estimate - glmer$b1) / glmer$se1) < 1e-5
#> [1] TRUE
